hints: Notice the parent nucleus $^{185}_{79}\text{Au}$ starts with nucleon number 185 and proton number 79.
Recall what an alpha particle carries away: nucleon number 4 and proton number 2 as $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$.
Subtract the alpha-particle numbers from both parent numbers to conserve total nucleon number and charge.
walkthrough: Identify the parent numbers: top number is nucleon number $A=185$ and bottom number is proton number $Z=79$.
State the alpha-decay rule: emission of $^{4}_{2}\text{He}$ removes 4 from the nucleon number and 2 from the proton number.
Match $181$ and $77$ to the table. This is option C.

options.A: Nucleon number 183 is only 2 less than 185 and proton number is unchanged, which does not match loss of an alpha particle.
options.B: Proton number 77 is correct for alpha decay, but nucleon number 183 is only reduced by 2 instead of by 4.
options.C: An alpha particle removes 4 nucleons and 2 protons, so $185-4=181$ and $79-2=77$.
options.D: Nucleon number 181 is correct, but proton number 75 is reduced by 4 instead of by 2.
